q:
Everyone kept saying that the typical symptoms will be worse with twins and once I entered my second trimester it will be fine.

It’s not fine…my symptoms are actually worse now
cx: First pregnancy, twins, 13+5 weeks.

q: I said I’d do it but he said “no, you just *sit* *there.”*
cx: 15 weeks with her second and a 21-month-old, very sick; husband covering childcare.

q: Yesterday he asked about getting weekend help for the duration of my pregnancy, which I wasn’t keen on.
cx: They already use a sitter three weekdays plus her mother and father-in-law.

q: My first pregnancy also sucked, but it didn’t impact his life (I was just sick all the time and he would still go out with friends and do his hobby). Now he needs to pick up parenting slack and it’s throwing him for a loop.
cx: Why the second pregnancy is harder on her husband.

q: I definitely think I let myself get resentful, but it’s on me for not asking for more earlier.
cx: After commenters' perspective on her husband.

q: I feel like I was following medical guidance and now the internet is making me feel like I messed up.
cx: Nine weeks, dyed her hair after reading her OB's handout.

q: But then a friend sent me a bunch of stuff online saying to avoid hair dye in the first trimester and especially to avoid ammonia-containing dyes.
cx: Her OB's handout had said hair dye was considered safe.

q: This is my second pregnancy so I’m running around after a toddler which is exhausting in itself.
cx: Third trimester, trying to deep-clean before the baby.

q: I feel like I’m drowning in house work that just gets messy / dirty the second I’ve cleaned.
cx: Nesting with a toddler.

q: She then set a meeting with me the following day and told me that I needed a note from my OB before they could continue to accommodate me any further (highlighting what I can and cannot do).
cx: At 14+5, after asking her supervisor not to add work.

q: At first my work was willing to make some accommodations for me upon me asking, and even allowed me 40 hours of unpaid time off additionally because I was calling off so much from my nausea.
cx: What her employer offered earlier in the pregnancy.

q: He said he couldn’t write me a note outlining what I can and cannot do at my job, only that I stated that I could not perform specific tasks because I guess businesses have tried to sue them over Drs notes before?
cx: Her OB's answer when asked for a work note.

q: For clarification, my issues are with my mental fog and fatigue. My job requires a lot of mental work and remembering policies and processing things correctly or timely otherwise it affects other people outside of what I’m doing. I just feel like I’m at a 40 expected to be at a 100.
cx: Government casework job, short-staffed and on a hiring freeze.

q: The only problem is my insurance is through my job and I don’t think I would be eligible for any type of disability benefits if so or my insurance. I’m not meeting with HR until later this month to talk about FMLA since they’re on vacation.
cx: Weighing a drop to part-time.

q: I’m starting to feel like I’m just going to stick it out until I get fired from falling behind on my workload because it’s so hard and stressful to keep up. Non pregnant me could do everything and then some.
cx: Falling behind at work in the second trimester.

q: My point was that it feels like there’s no help out there, that I don’t feel like I’m being listen to or my concerns are taken seriously and other countries have so many other benefits in place for women this early on.
cx: US, replying to commenters in a long thread.

q: I wanted to have more kids, now I’m questioning whether it would be worth it.
cx: After her employer and OB would not help.

q: It just felt like he wasn’t listening to me or at least trying to understand what was going on. I had issues the first time I saw him to and the appointment today sent me home in tears, it just felt so dismissive.
cx: Her OB cut her off and recorded symptoms she says she didn't report.

q: Would it be pathetic of me to request a shorter working week? I am due to be on AL at the start of June anyway until my mat leave kicks in in July. I just feel guilty taking time off but I am burning out quick.
cx: UK, 28 weeks, two hours' driving a day, cannot work from home.

q: My husband has been away since January and isn't back until the end of this month
cx: Third trimester mostly on her own.

q: I do end up feeling guilty because I know people complain about restrictions from my pregnancy risk assessment 🤣. Arseholes.
cx: Colleagues' reaction to her workplace adjustments.

q: I am trying to carry a few days over as much as I can of annual leave so I can spend more paid days with the bambino.
cx: Banking annual leave to extend paid time after the birth.

q: I have an appointment booked today and I will see if I can get 3 days in a week. I just feel so impertinent advocating for myself.
cx: Asking for a shorter week at 28 weeks.

q: My mom then says to me “yeah you’re tired alright, what are you going to do when you have a newborn baby?”
cx: End of the second trimester, after asking for a quiet birthday weekend.

q: Every week I hear a complaint about the cost of things for the shower. How things on my registry are too out of her price range. The cake is too expensive.
cx: Her mother insisted on hosting the baby shower.

q: Eventually it lead into me saying how I’ve been tired and hurting the last few days. Her response, “oh that’s not good, why?”
cx: A phone call with her mother.

q: There’s been no babies in the family since I was born, and having to explain a car seat carrier has been like trying to deconstruct the Davinci code.
cx: Explaining baby gear to her mother.

q: The idea of having two under two feels overwhelming, especially when so many mothers in that stage seem constantly exhausted, stretched thin, and struggling to keep up.
cx: Unexpectedly pregnant with a 1.5-year-old; polished wording, possibly tool-written; one voice.

q: labor and delivery told me to not come in unless I couldn’t bear to talk through them
cx: At 37 weeks, three weeks of on-off contractions.
r: medical (unit includes screening for a condition, mental-health wording)

q: I just don’t want to go in to be turned away again that’s what is making me not want to go in.
cx: Waiting on a test result and on stronger contractions.

q: I'm likely having this baby in late June and then my husband will be changing jobs and have about 6 weeks off from work starting in mid September. We'd love (in theory) to take a trip during that time.
cx: Planning around her husband's gap between jobs.

q: my midwives want me to set up a birth plan but I really don’t feel it’s worth it when I’m sure it’ll get ruined with an induced C section due to something I can’t control.
cx: First-time mother at 20 weeks, worried about weight-related conditions.
r: medical condition and procedure (weight, induction, caesarean)

q: I feel guilty that they will be so far from their first grandchild, but I’ll do my best to go to England a lot to visit!
cx: English woman living in South Korea, planning how to tell her parents.
